bull_bear.body:
- Established terminal position at Kandla Port, a location private oil companies use to optimise PAN-India logistics and transportation costs for petroleum products
- Long-standing leasehold tank-farm infrastructure at a major port, an asset base that new entrants can only replicate by securing scarce port land
- Diversified customer base spanning petrochemicals, chemicals, edible oils and petroleum, serving both importers and exporters
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Expired Kandla land leases with Deendayal Port Trust, with renewal sub judice before the Supreme Court — Both terminal land leases with DPT have expired and MD&A states renewal is very crucial to keep business continuity at Kandla; the matter is sub judice with the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Because the terminals are the Company's only revenue source, an adverse outcome threatens the operating base itself, and the Company has made its modernisation capex conditional on the renewal.
- Qualified audit opinion over the unprovided DPT transfer fee and lease-rent liability — The statutory auditors qualified their opinion on the FY26 financial statements: DPT has demanded transfer/upfront fees for change of name and an increase in lease rent on revision of rates for the leasehold lands. No provision (including interest) or adjustment has been made because the incremental liability and the impact on leased assets are not currently ascertainable; depreciation on assets built on leasehold land and right-of-use lease assets continue to be recognised on previously determined terms. The auditors state the final outcome may impact profits as well as right-of-use lease assets and lease liabilities.
- Single-asset, single-location, single-segment concentration — The Company operates in only one segment - bulk liquid storage - and currently derives its share of revenue solely from its bulk liquid terminals at Kandla, Gujarat. MD&A states that being majorly dependent on these terminals exposes it to risks particular to that business and environment, with no geographic or segment diversification to absorb a shock. The concentration deepened after the multimodal logistics subsidiary was sold during the year.
- Intensifying competition and overcapacity at Kandla eroding utilisation — Increased storage tank capacities at Kandla Port by various terminal operators have reduced utilisation in general and increased competition. The AVTL consortium aggregating Aegis, Vopak & Friends holds about 0.8 mMT of tankage in 240 tanks, with Aegis holding a further 0.2 mMT at Mumbai, which management says gives them leverage to dominate the Kandla market. One more chemical handling terminal was added at Kandla, shifting customer preferences.
- Lease-rental cost uncertainty compressing the bottom line — The Directors' Report states that uncertainty in respect of lease rentals payable to Kandla Port could continue to affect the bottom line - an unquantified and unprovided cost overhang on a business whose principal operating input is leased port land.
- Competing port infrastructure at Mundra and Hazira drawing away cargo — The Directors' Report flags that development of better infrastructure and reduced demurrages at nearby ports such as Mundra and Hazira may affect the business of the Company - a structural threat to Kandla's catchment that the Company cannot influence.
- Shift in customer packaging away from bulk export parcels — Exports were reduced by 28% during the year mainly due to an increase in flexi and ISO tank requirement instead of bulk export. This is a mode shift in how liquids move, not a cyclical dip, and it structurally shrinks the addressable bulk-export volume for terminal operators.
- Regulatory, policy, trade and geo-political exposure with clearance dependency — MD&A Risks and Concerns lists regulatory or policy change pertaining to the business, economic parameters, trade policy and geo-political factors, market risk, governmental clearances and approvals, and credit risk as difficult to foresee. For a port-based liquid storage operator, dependence on governmental clearances and approvals is a live operating constraint rather than boilerplate. The Company states it has a Risk Management Policy and follows business and risk mitigation practices.

outlook.body: Expansion plans are stated qualitatively and are contingent on the lease position at Kandla. The Company has plans to invest in safety and modernisation such as a Tankfarm Management System (TFMS) at the existing terminals, but explicitly only after renewal of the lease(s) with Deendayal Port Trust (DPT) - both terminal land leases have expired and the renewal dispute is sub judice before the Supreme Court, so this spend has no announced timeline or quantum. outlook.body:
- Private-sector bulk liquid storage acts as a dominant logistics partner in the supply chain for primary manufacturers and downstream units across petrochemicals, chemicals, synthetic fibre, edible/non-edible oil refining, power, food processing and pharmaceuticals
- The 'Make in India' programme and increased domestic demand are expected to drive regular growth in the industry, with port-led modernisation of major Indian ports supporting rising handling volumes year on year
- Domestic private-sector oil companies are increasingly hiring storage tanks at port locations to optimise logistics and transportation costs of petroleum products PAN-India; management expects this trend to continue and volumes to increase, as surplus refining capacity means imported crude and refined products must be moved inland from port locations
- Increasing urbanisation and rising per capita disposable income support a strong growth outlook for several key end-use industries; liquid bulk trade volumes are set to grow at a rapid pace
- Higher imports of raw materials for the pharma industry have created opportunity for chemical storage terminals
- Government thrust towards domestic manufacturing is expected to redefine product flow patterns, and export volumes are expected to keep increasing to address the production-versus-domestic-demand mismatch
- Adverse driver: increased storage tank capacities at Kandla by various terminal operators have reduced utilisation generally and intensified competition; the AVTL consortium (Aegis, Vopak & Friends) aggregates about 0.8 mMT of tankage in 240 tanks and Aegis holds a further 0.2 mMT at Mumbai, giving them leverage to dominate the Kandla market
- Adverse driver: exports fell 28% during the year as customers shifted to flexi and ISO tanks instead of bulk export, and one more chemical handling terminal was added at Kandla shifting customer preferences
- Adverse driver: uncertainty over lease rentals payable to Kandla Port could continue to affect the bottom line, and better infrastructure and reduced demurrages at nearby ports such as Mundra and Hazira may affect the business (the Mundra/Hazira point is sourced from the Directors' Report text carried in the risks_esg bundle of the same annual report)

- Improve commercial utilisation of existing tankage to lift revenue, the stated driver of the FY26 revenue increase alongside higher imports
- Operate as a focused single-segment bulk liquid storage business following the exit from multimodal logistics via the sale of Kesar Multimodal Logistics Ltd to DP World
- Retain and engage a small, trained workforce as a competitive differentiator, with focus on high performance, talent retention and employee engagement

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion plans are stated qualitatively and are contingent on the lease position at Kandla. The Company has plans to invest in safety and modernisation such as a Tankfarm Management System (TFMS) at the existing terminals, but explicitly only after renewal of the lease(s) with Deendayal Port Trust (DPT) - both terminal land leases have expired and the renewal dispute is sub judice before the Supreme Court, so this spend has no announced timeline or quantum. Separately, the Company has a plan to set up a Bulk Terminal at other locations based on opportunity and market, again with no named site, capex figure or commissioning date. No rupee capex quantum, capital-commitment note or segment capital-expenditure line was supplied in this bundle. Capacity is described only as throughput: the Kandla terminals handled 0.62 MMTPA in FY2025-26, with revenue growth attributed to increased imports and better commercial utilisation of tanks.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Established terminal position at Kandla Port, a location private oil companies use to optimise PAN-India logistics and transportation costs for petroleum products
- Long-standing leasehold tank-farm infrastructure at a major port, an asset base that new entrants can only replicate by securing scarce port land
- Diversified customer base spanning petrochemicals, chemicals, edible oils and petroleum, serving both importers and exporters

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Expired Kandla land leases with Deendayal Port Trust, with renewal sub judice before the Supreme Court — Both terminal land leases with DPT have expired and MD&A states renewal is very crucial to keep business continuity at Kandla; the matter is sub judice with the Hon'ble Supreme Court. Because the terminals are the Company's only revenue source, an adverse outcome threatens the operating base itself, and the Company has made its modernisation capex conditional on the renewal.
- Qualified audit opinion over the unprovided DPT transfer fee and lease-rent liability — The statutory auditors qualified their opinion on the FY26 financial statements: DPT has demanded transfer/upfront fees for change of name and an increase in lease rent on revision of rates for the leasehold lands. No provision (including interest) or adjustment has been made because the incremental liability and the impact on leased assets are not currently ascertainable; depreciation on assets built on leasehold land and right-of-use lease assets continue to be recognised on previously determined terms. The auditors state the final outcome may impact profits as well as right-of-use lease assets and lease liabilities.
- Single-asset, single-location, single-segment concentration — The Company operates in only one segment - bulk liquid storage - and currently derives its share of revenue solely from its bulk liquid terminals at Kandla, Gujarat. MD&A states that being majorly dependent on these terminals exposes it to risks particular to that business and environment, with no geographic or segment diversification to absorb a shock. The concentration deepened after the multimodal logistics subsidiary was sold during the year.
- Intensifying competition and overcapacity at Kandla eroding utilisation — Increased storage tank capacities at Kandla Port by various terminal operators have reduced utilisation in general and increased competition. The AVTL consortium aggregating Aegis, Vopak & Friends holds about 0.8 mMT of tankage in 240 tanks, with Aegis holding a further 0.2 mMT at Mumbai, which management says gives them leverage to dominate the Kandla market. One more chemical handling terminal was added at Kandla, shifting customer preferences.
- Lease-rental cost uncertainty compressing the bottom line — The Directors' Report states that uncertainty in respect of lease rentals payable to Kandla Port could continue to affect the bottom line - an unquantified and unprovided cost overhang on a business whose principal operating input is leased port land.
- Competing port infrastructure at Mundra and Hazira drawing away cargo — The Directors' Report flags that development of better infrastructure and reduced demurrages at nearby ports such as Mundra and Hazira may affect the business of the Company - a structural threat to Kandla's catchment that the Company cannot influence.
- Shift in customer packaging away from bulk export parcels — Exports were reduced by 28% during the year mainly due to an increase in flexi and ISO tank requirement instead of bulk export. This is a mode shift in how liquids move, not a cyclical dip, and it structurally shrinks the addressable bulk-export volume for terminal operators.
- Regulatory, policy, trade and geo-political exposure with clearance dependency — MD&A Risks and Concerns lists regulatory or policy change pertaining to the business, economic parameters, trade policy and geo-political factors, market risk, governmental clearances and approvals, and credit risk as difficult to foresee. For a port-based liquid storage operator, dependence on governmental clearances and approvals is a live operating constraint rather than boilerplate. The Company states it has a Risk Management Policy and follows business and risk mitigation practices.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Secure renewal of the expired Kandla terminal land leases with Deendayal Port Trust - management calls renewal crucial to business continuity and makes its modernisation spend conditional on it
- Invest in safety and modernisation of the existing tank farms, specifically a Tankfarm Management System (TFMS), once the DPT leases are renewed
- Set up a Bulk Terminal at other locations based on opportunity and market, diversifying away from single-location dependence on Kandla
- Improve commercial utilisation of existing tankage to lift revenue, the stated driver of the FY26 revenue increase alongside …

hero.oneLiner: Kesar Terminals & Infrastructure operates bulk liquid storage and handling terminals at Kandla (Deendayal) Port in Gujarat, which handled a throughput of 0.62 MMTPA in FY2025-26.
